guide.summary: Own Greenhouse partner app for customers (partner acceptance); Prototype with Composio managed app (approval path unconfirmed). Where the path is unconfirmed, the agent did not find it in the provider's docs.
guide.verdict: Own Greenhouse partner app for customers (partner acceptance).

composio.note: Composio lists Greenhouse under managed OAuth, so prototypes need no Greenhouse registration. For launch under your own brand, use a custom auth config with your partner credentials.

need_own_app.answer: Not for a prototype, since Composio's managed app works. For production under your own brand, with dedicated quota or custom scopes, you need your own Greenhouse partner credentials, which require partner acceptance.
reasons: Users see your app name instead of 'Composio wants to access your account'
Managed apps share quota across all Composio users; your own app gets dedicated quota
Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum trigger polling interval

prerequisites.title: Signed Greenhouse partnership agreement
prerequisites.detail: Required before you can create an OAuth app or start the partner OAuth process. Greenhouse may refuse your application.

prerequisites.title: Website with Privacy Policy and a mutual customer
prerequisites.detail: You need an active website with a Privacy Policy, and at least one mutual customer named in the request.

prerequisites.title: Integration details and 128x128 logo
prerequisites.detail: Prepare integration name, environment, scopes, redirect URI and a 128x128 logo shown on the consent screen.

prerequisites.title: Customer plan and permissions
prerequisites.detail: Harvest v3 partner integrations are available on Core, Plus and Pro tiers. Setup needs a Site Admin or a user who can manage all API credentials.

steps.title: Submit the integration request form
steps.detail: Fill out Greenhouse's integration request form with your integration and goals, naming at least one mutual customer.

steps.title: Wait for monthly partner review
steps.detail: Applications are reviewed on the first Monday of the month; the Partnerships team replies within 7 business days. Out-of-cycle review is generally only for urgent mutual customer needs.
steps.done_when: You are confirmed and invited to sign the agreement.

steps.title: Sign the partnership agreement
steps.detail: Sign the Greenhouse Partnership Agreement after being invited.

steps.title: Draft credential request details
steps.detail: Prepare integration name, environment, minimal required scopes, and redirect URI. Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard.
steps.done_when: Request text is ready to send.

steps.title: Email Partner Support for credentials
steps.detail: Send the details and 128x128 logo to Greenhouse Partner Support. Greenhouse issues the Client ID and Secret.
steps.done_when: You hold a Client ID and Client Secret.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create a custom auth config for the greenhouse toolkit using your client ID and secret via Composio's API.
steps.done_when: Auth config exists and a test connection works.

steps.title: Connect with Composio managed auth
steps.detail: Use the Composio-managed Greenhouse auth config; no client ID needed.
steps.done_when: A user can authorize Greenhouse through Composio.

traps.title: The authorization code lasts 1 minute and must be
traps.detail: The authorization code lasts 1 minute and must be exchanged quickly; the page gives no testing-mode-specific lifetime.

traps.title: Refresh tokens last 14 days; if unused for 14
traps.detail: Refresh tokens last 14 days; if unused for 14 days, the user must repeat the whole authorization flow.

traps.title: Application is not an approval
traps.detail: Submitting the form does not confirm the partnership, and you must wait for official confirmation before the integration steps. Not all submissions are accepted.

traps.title: Refresh token expires after 14 days unused
traps.detail: Access tokens last 1 hour and the authorization code lasts 1 minute. If a refresh token goes unused for 14 days, the user must redo the whole authorization flow.

traps.title: Testing environment is sandbox only
traps.detail: A testing client works only in your own sandbox; choose production to be live for mutual customers.

traps.title: Redirect URI must match exactly
traps.detail: A redirect_uri not registered for your client ID returns an invalid_request 400 error. Requesting scopes not permitted for your client gives invalid_scope.

traps.title: Authorizer permissions affect API calls
traps.detail: A 403 can occur if the user who authorized lacks the needed in-app Greenhouse permissions.

traps.title: Managed app shares quota and branding
traps.detail: Managed apps share quota across all Composio users and show 'Composio wants to access your account' during OAuth.

blockers.symptom: Partner application not accepted or no reply
blockers.what_it_means: Greenhouse reviews all submissions but does not accept all of them.
blockers.what_to_do: Wait for the monthly review and 7 business days. Email partneronboarding@greenhouse.io for an out-of-cycle review only if a mutual customer has an urgent need.
blockers.agent_can_help: Draft the out-of-cycle review email with the customer's reasoning.

blockers.symptom: invalid_scope error or 401 on token exchange
blockers.what_it_means: The client requested scopes it is not permitted to use.
blockers.what_to_do: Ask Partner Support to add the needed scopes to your client.
blockers.agent_can_help: Compare requested scopes with the scopes registered for your client.

items.reason: Quote states that every submission is reviewed but not all are accepted.
Quote says Greenhouse reviews the application for program alignment and then invites the applicant to sign the partnership agreement.
Quote says Greenhouse provides the Client ID and Secret; the absence of self-service registration is consistent with the quotes.
Quote states an active website with a Privacy Policy is required to apply.
Quote states at least one mutual customer is required for the request to be submitted.
Quote is only the header 'Provide Information: Tell us:'; the listed items (name, environment, scopes, redirect URIs, logo) are not in the quotes.
Quote states testing is only the developer's own sandbox and production is live for mutual customers.
Quote requires a 128x128 logo and says customers see it when authorizing.
Quote states scope is required and is a space-separated list of needed permissions.
Quote states the Partnerships team reaches out within 7 business days of the monthly review.
Quote states integration requests are reviewed monthly on the first Monday.
Quote says to email partneronboarding@greenhouse.io with reasoning after submitting for an out-of-cycle review.
Quote says applicants must wait to be officially confirmed before the integration steps; not all requests are accepted.
Quote states availability for new subscription tiers Core, Plus, and Pro.
Quote states the permission requirement: Site Admins or users who can manage all organization API credentials.
Quote states the partner determines where the connection starts and whether a Site Admin or standard user completes setup.
Quote states the access token lifetime is 1 hour.
Quote gives the mismatch error message but not the invalid_request error code or HTTP 400 status.
Quote gives the scopes-not-permitted message but does not name the invalid_scope error or say it is returned on redirect.
Quote says the user may lack in-app permissions, but does not mention a 403 Forbidden error.
Quotes require a signed partnership agreement before creating an OAuth app, and Greenhouse reviews applications and invites signing.
Quote 'Every submission will be reviewed' supports that review always applies.
Quotes support the form, monthly review, and signing steps, but not the credential request or directory listing steps or their order.
Quotes say the review checks alignment with the program; they do not mention checking data need or the listing.
Quotes state the active website with Privacy Policy and at least one mutual customer requirements.
Quotes state Site Admin permissions and that the partner decides whether a Site Admin or standard user completes setup.
Quote states testing is only in the developer's own sandbox before production.
Quote says no OAuth app registration or client credentials are needed, but does not say the client registers itself automatically.
Quotes support no registration for Composio and the review requirement, but contain no monthly-cycle or 7-business-day (about 10 days) timing.
